newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-Warne takes two wickets in Shield match.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Warne takes two wickets in Shield match.

text.p: Australia leg-spinner Shane Warne survived the first major examination of his injured finger ahead of this month's first test against West Indies by taking two wickets for Victoria in a Sheffield Shield match on Friday.
Warne bowled 20 overs at the Sydney Cricket Ground in his heaviest match workload this season after undergoing surgery in May to repair ligament damage in his bowling hand.
With the first test against West Indies starting in a fortnight's time, Victoria's four-day match against New South Wales in Sydney is a vital test of Warne's fitness.
On his first-class debut as Victoria state captain, Warne claimed the wickets of tail-enders Anthony Stuart and Stuart MacGill after New South Wales won the toss and chose to bat.
At close of play on the first day, Victoria were 68 for one in reply to New South Wales' first innings total of 264.
Warne finished with two for 40, including eight maidens, and took a sharp, head-high catch at first slip to dismiss tail-ender David Freedman from the bowling of Brad Williams.
"I thought I bowled pretty well and it was good to bowl 20 overs," Warne told reporters. "They came out pretty well and I didn't bowl much short stuff.
"The real key is how my finger pulls up tomorrow. Hopefully it pulls up well and I'll be able to bowl again in a couple of days' time."
Warne produced enough spin to have Stuart stumped by Darren Berry on the last ball before tea and then trapped MacGill leg before wicket with his flipper.
Warne, whose test haul stands at 207 wickets in 44 matches, was badly missed by Australia during recent unsuccessful tours of India and Sri Lanka.
In Brisbane, Queensland need to score only 100 runs on the fourth and final day of their match to beat Tasmania.
Queensland scored 244 for a first innings lead of 76 before Scott Muller took four for 35 and Adam Dale four for 44 to dismiss Tasmania for 176 in their second innings.
Queensland openers Trevor Barsby and Matthew Hayden reached the close of play without incident to leave their side three full sessions to score the necessary runs.
